title: Win back churned customers with something new
decision_task: Whether to spend effort reactivating past customers before or alongside acquiring new ones, and what to send.
applies_when: A churned base that is large relative to monthly new signups
Meaningful new value shipped since they left
Consent or a lawful basis to contact them
exclusions: No consent (never cold-email past users through ClimbOS)
Nothing has changed since they left
They left because they were the wrong fit
Very few churned customers: a personal note is cheaper than a sequence
required_inputs: A trial-restart or offer mechanism if used
evidence_requirements: Whether each still uses a free tier
List of changes shipped since each cohort left
missing_data_behavior: No consent to contact past customers: not eligible; never cold-email them.
No change since they left: not eligible.
alternatives_when_constrained: Missing data: owner exports past customers and marks reasons
Low volume: personal email from the owner's own mailbox
No integration: manual send from the owner's mailbox

decision_branches.if: Churned base is large relative to new signups and value shipped since
decision_branches.then: A short win-back naming the specific change.
A personal note from the owner.

implementation_steps: Segment churned payers still active on free vs fully inactive
For still-active: time-limited paid-feature trial restart tied to a major launch
For inactive: slow sequence each showing one specific new capability, with occasional trial restarts
Hold out a share where volume allows
Compare expected reactivations times value with the same effort spent on new-user conversion
dependencies: A specific product change to name
metrics: Paid reactivation rate per segment vs holdout
guardrails: Consent and suppression checked before every send
Claims about what is new must be true and specific
observation_window: One launch cycle plus the next renewal of reactivated customers.
stop_conditions: Unsubscribes or complaints rise above normal
Reactivated customers churn again in their first term at the original rate
review_triggers: Owner corrects an input this playbook relies on
A metric or guardrail crosses its bound
The underlying source or platform rule changes
climbos_location: shared/playbooks/contracts.ts PB-lifecycle-email ('lapsed' moment) as a win-back variant; retention branch in diagnosis.ts.

interpretation: INTERPRETATION: Reactivation competes with acquisition for the same owner hours; it deserves a slot when the churned base is big and the product changed.
proposed_climbos_rule: PROPOSED RULE: When retention is the constraint and consented churned contacts exceed new signups for the period, PB-lifecycle-email's lapsed moment must be considered and its message must name a specific change since the customer left.
disagreements: None material. Her comparison is illustrative and stays out of forecasts.

hypothetical_evaluation_cases.label: hypothetical
expected_behavior: Proposes a two-segment win-back led by the new feature, with a holdout
Puts trial restarts on the still-active segment
Does not forecast with the 1–2% figure
hard_failure: Generic 'we miss you' blast to all
Uses her illustrative 1–2% as a benchmark

notes: Proposed reference contract. Not executable; does not authorize publishing, sending or spending. Numbers in source references are dated author figures, never forecasts.
